acceptance: The test's duration distribution on hosted runners over at least 10 recent runs is recorded on this item.
The test finishes in under half its timeout on hosted runners in 10 consecutive medium-tier runs after the change, with the same assertions.
A timeout in the MCP run fails with a message that names the timeout, not a KeyError.
context:
2026-11-17 TODO review. Measurement source for the decision gate and acceptance: pytest `--durations` output or junit timings in the medium-tier job logs of green CI runs on develop and PRs (gh run view --log of the medium-test shard that ran the test), not local timings. Verification rubric: pass = (1) at least 10 pre-change runner durations recorded here with run ids; (2) after the change, 10 consecutive medium-tier runs that executed this test show it under 30 s each, run ids recorded; (3) a unit-level test or forced timeout shows the MCP-run timeout surfacing as a named timeout failure, not KeyError 'mcp_metadata'; (4) the CLI-versus-MCP config-block equality assertion is unchanged. Fail = a raised timeout without the shrink attempt recorded, a skip/flaky mark/known-failures entry, or a weakened assertion. Base guardrails: linked worktree only; heavy test tiers only through lock-taking entry points; one PR; comment policy; no changelog fragment unless user-facing behaviour changes.

2026-11-17 measured and root-caused. Runner durations from medium-shard junit of 12 trunk runs (44132228157 .. 43879705406): shipped-defaults min 28.4 / median 42.1 / max 57.3 s; compression-disabled 11.2 / 15.1 / 21.4 s; polars-df 28.2 / 38.0 / 49.2 s (timeout 60 s, medium tier -n 5). Local split under the host lock: shipped-defaults CLI 13.5 s + MCP 28.5 s; compression-disabled CLI 17.5 s + MCP 4.0 s. cProfile of the MCP half: 14.3 of 17.3 s in TPC-H data generation, all in `_run_streaming_dbgen`, which with compression on runs dbgen once per table (8 processes, serially). Each dbgen start costs about 1.6 s locally regardless of table size (region, 384 bytes, also 1.6 s), while one dbgen run for all tables takes 1.6 s total. Stdout and file output are byte-identical for all 8 tables at SF 0.01. Decision (shrink the work, not raise the timeout): stream per table only above SF 1, where avoiding the uncompressed temporary files matters; at SF <= 1 a compressed run uses the single dbgen invocation and compresses afterwards. This speeds up every compressed small-scale TPC-H run, not only the test. Also: a missing `mcp_metadata` now fails with the full response instead of KeyError.
description:
On 2026-11-16 the medium tier (shard 0) of CI run 43785546346 failed twice in a row, on the first attempt and on a re-run of the failed jobs, in `tests/integration/test_cli_mcp_result_parity.py::test_cli_and_mcp_record_the_same_config_block_for_the_same_request[shipped-defaults]`. The pull request (#4253) changes only an agent doc and a refusal message. First attempt: `KeyError: 'mcp_metadata'` after `Benchmark execution failed (DataLoadingError)` and a pytest-timeout banner; second attempt: `Failed: Timeout (>60.0s) from pytest-timeout`. On the same branch the test passes locally on an Apple silicon host in 21 seconds (the whole file in 44 seconds). The test was added by #4228 on 2026-11-14. Other pull requests' CI failures in the same hours were in other jobs, so it is not known how often this one fails.

Likely cause, not confirmed: the case runs a real benchmark through both the CLI and the MCP entry point, and a hosted runner takes about three times as long as the local host, which crosses the 60-second per-test timeout. The KeyError on the first attempt looks like the same timeout surfacing as a missing key after the MCP run was cut off.

Decision gate: measure first. Read the durations of this test from recent green medium-tier runs. If it routinely takes more than about 40 seconds on runners, shrink what it runs (smaller scale factor or fewer queries, keeping the config-block comparison it exists for) rather than raise the timeout; raise the timeout only if the work cannot be reduced.

Guardrails: do not mark the test flaky, skip it on CI, or add it to the preflight known-failures list to get green; the parity it checks is the point. Do not weaken the assertion to tolerate a missing `mcp_metadata` key.
